task.title: Web status column administration panel
task.description:
Add column management to the web board, building on the read-only vocabulary rendering that the custom-status-columns story ships (GET /api/vocabulary, vocabularyHead in TasksDocument, columns derived from the vocabulary).

## Endpoints (REST shape matching /api/tasks)

- POST /api/vocabulary/statuses {"status","label","tags","before"|"after","expectedHead"}
- PATCH /api/vocabulary/statuses/{status} {"name"?,"label"?,"tags"?,"expectedHead"}
- DELETE /api/vocabulary/statuses/{status} {"into","expectedHead"} (a body on DELETE is deliberate: a deletion is meaningless without a destination)
- PUT /api/vocabulary/order {"statuses":[...],"expectedHead"} (a drag-reorder is one gesture, one intent)

Every mutation answers with the full vocabulary document.

## Queue and conflict rules (binding)

- Vocabulary mutations live OUTSIDE the optimistic mutation queue: the panel disables its controls, sends synchronously with expectedHead = the vocabulary head, and re-renders columns from the response. A rollback that repaints the whole board is worse than the latency the queue would hide.
- Quiescence: a vocabulary mutation is not sent while pendingIntents is non-empty (pending task intents may carry statuses the change retires); the save control reports "finishing pending changes" until the queue drains.
- stale-write (409): refetch /api/vocabulary and report "the vocabulary changed in another clone; review and retry." No re-base, no retry loop -- a vocabulary decision is a human decision.
- Update docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-06-optimistic-web-mutation-queue-design.md with a "Vocabulary mutations are outside the queue" section stating these rules.

Arity enforcement and validation reuse core.Vocabulary.Validate() so web and CLI share messages. Tag semantics (default/next/done), delete-with-destination, and rename-chain behavior are defined by the CLI story -- this panel is strictly a second surface over the same ledger operations.

## Shipped (2026-08-13)

Two PRs, each through an adversarial execution-verified review:

- **PR #92 (endpoints).** All four routes as specified, answering the full vocabulary document; stale expectedHead -> 409 with the current vocabulary attached (only on stale-write). The CLI status verbs were refactored into shared planners (planStatusAdd/Rename/... over a statusScope), proven byte-identical to main by a two-binary harness over the whole verb family; PATCH emits rename+relabel+tags as one pack reusing the CLI emission, verified to replay across divergent two-clone sync. Web mutations write the ledger only (guidelines settle on the next CLI touch; docs-refresh-incomplete warning), publish via watcher nudge or inline push. Review round 1 blockers fixed: an origin push REFUSAL was silently swallowed (result-reported, not error-reported), and expectedHead was checked but not CAS-enforced (a wedged write could merge two authors' renames into an alias chain neither chose) -- fixed by threading expectedHead down as the ref transaction's old-value via WriteConfigOperationOnto; a lost seed race now returns stale-write with exactly one reachable genesis root. Two-round review record on the PR.
- **PR #93 (panel).** A Statuses disclosure region in the board header: add/edit/delete-with-destination/reorder, tags from the server, delete pricing (tasks moved / claimable), warnings surfaced. The binding rules verified on the wire in headless Chrome: mutations outside the optimistic queue behind a single funnel; quiescence awaits the task queue's drain promises (105-drag starvation probe: bounded, honest, no livelock); 409 is terminal (adopt-from-refusal, no retry); reconciliation through the existing vocabulary notice -- card node identity held across mutation + polls. The task-queue refactor (entry.settled) A/B tested byte-identical against a main-built binary across five race/failure scenarios. Spec doc gained the "Vocabulary mutations are outside the queue" section, including the deliberate one-directional quiescence asymmetry. One-round review + polish (rename reported under the new name, defensive drag-state clear, comment corrections).

**Noted residuals (accepted):** whole-board reorder can renumber past a concurrent fractional status move (deterministic, convergent, losing op recorded with its inverse); Administrable gate unreachable in production (single call site supplies all four); removed-column drop targets keep the generic refusal message until reload. Renaming onto a retired name re-points the alias chain -- pre-existing on main, filed as WB-01KZXNG3PQVYJ3FZEFSPJRMA9E.
